name: American exceptionalism
summary: American exceptionalism holds that the United States is distinctive and exemplary, founded on liberty, equality, individualism, popular government and religious faith, and that it has a special role as a beacon or leader for the world. Adherents see it as a model nation rather than one bound by Old World class divisions.
scope: The mainstream patriotic version from Winthrop and Jefferson through Tocqueville, Lipset and Reagan, in which the US is a free, religious, market-minded republic with a global leadership role. It is not a full program, so many economic and social answers are 0 or low; it excludes the Marxist and postnationalist critical senses of the term.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; inferred indifference.

elective-rulers.rationale: Exceptionalism is rooted in a republic founded on popular government and rejection of hereditary rule.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the American tradition pairs majority rule with individual rights, with no veto for a dissenting member.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The founding narrative of the Declaration of Independence justifies removing rulers who violate rights and trust.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: the American model is a separated-powers republic, not parliamentary supremacy.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents are split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: mainstream patriotic Americans accept humane animal use; the issue is not central to the idea.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Winthrop teaches that the rich are bound to show mercy and liberality to the poor within the covenant community.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: Reagan-style patriotism calls for civic engagement and participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Lipset treats American individualism and anti-statism as the norm, not a pacified, class-ordered society.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: exceptionalism holds that the US lacks Old World class order; the thesis is a critics claim.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: Reagan stresses open markets and trade as sources of prosperity.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reagan celebrates the immigrant who becomes fully American; offices are open to naturalized citizens in the tradition, except the presidency.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-help individualism favours self-reliance, but exceptionalism also supports American leadership through aid; split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: US-centred foreign policy treats force-based revision of borders as illegitimate.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Reagan frames America as open to all who join it, with equal citizenship.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: Reagan and Cold War exceptionalism condemned totalitarianism of both kinds as enemies of freedom.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: the mainstream patriotic narrative accepts the standard historical account, though a Lost Cause minority dissents.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: the patriotic tradition of honoring the national past favours preservation.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Exceptionalism treats American liberal-democratic institutions as a model with universal appeal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the American tradition prizes civilian control of the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: anti-state individualism opposes state-paid wages for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition stresses family and faith but treats filial duty as a private matter.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the tradition prizes popular government and the elected citizen-officeholder over appointed mandarins.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred: the market-minded, open-economy outlook favours free sale of firms, though security carve-outs have wide support.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Split: the religious strand of the tradition resists easy divorce while the individualist strand favours personal freedom.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: the founders' republic gives representatives independent judgment and fixed terms rather than binding instruction.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Split: the anti-statist strand favours private accounts, but the tradition has accepted public pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: the Jeffersonian free-holder ideal and the market-minded republic rest on private ownership of land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the constitutional republic gives the legislature the power of the purse, which adherents treat as basic to self-government.

single-official-language.rationale: Split: English-only advocates cite a common civic language, while the tradition also prizes immigrant pluralism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's openness to immigrants and investment conflicts with a nationalist wish to protect land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the individualist, equal-opportunity outlook defines discrimination by treatment rather than outcome.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred: the tradition celebrates abundance and enterprise, so adherents see consumer prosperity as a good.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: Reagan's Farewell Address and the leadership role fit the Reagan Doctrine of backing anti-communist insurgents.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred: the tradition's self-determination ideals oppose coercion of allies, though the US has policed its own sphere.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from the anti-state, pro-business individualism that Lipset treats as defining; big donors are not seen as the main threat.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The idea says nothing on foreign funding; adherents are split between open-society and sovereignty views.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Reagan's farewell praises open immigration as a source of American strength, so relying on migrants is accepted; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from the individualist, free-market outlook that favours open property markets.

job-guarantee.rationale: Lipset describes distrust of the state and individualism as defining traits, which cuts against a state job guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: The American strand holds that spreading liberty serves peace and security, as in Wilsonian and Reagan-era policy.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from the covenant and rule-of-law tradition, which stresses duty to the republic's laws.

non-intervention.rationale: The idea gives the US a leading role in the world, and interventions for liberty are part of the tradition.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred from the individualist, anti-state outlook that is hostile to compulsory industrial unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The strand sees America as an open, free nation; conspiracy claims against a minority are not part of it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the religious and family-centred strand of the tradition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from the Jeffersonian view of accountable, popular government.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the free-market, open-trade outlook.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the tradition prizes lasting constitutional institutions and parties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Wikipedia notes American exceptionalism is tied to a view that the US stands apart from or above international rules; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by a civic creed of liberty open to immigrants, not by shared faith, though religion is prized.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The doctrine casts the US as a free republic that should lead as a beacon, never one that pays tribute, and Americans reject ritual submission to others.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed: the individualist, limited-government theme favours keeping money local, while the national idea favours a shared union, so adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine centres on private property and enterprise, so common ownership of the means of production is rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Reagan's Farewell Address and Cold War exceptionalism cast communism as a rival to the free world to be outlasted, though it is not a defining claim.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The doctrine is silent here; the anti-state strand prefers private provision, but patriotic adherents accept mixed arrangements.

religion-illusion.rationale: Winthrop's covenant and the doctrine's religious-faith theme treat religion as a lasting foundation of American life, not a consolation that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine celebrates a free market republic and its prosperity, though it does not use the Marxist framing of historical stages.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine holds that equality is secured within the existing system through liberty and law.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from its individualist, anti-state theme, which leaves housework and childcare to families and private arrangements.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: America is seen as a land open to immigrants, and the doctrine has no tradition of linguistic purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed: respect for law and covenant favours binding treaties, but the history of treaties with Native nations is contested among adherents.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The doctrine frames the nation as individualist and market-minded, with the nation-state as the unit, not communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the doctrine's emphasis on liberty and equal citizenship runs against state-steered settlement, although westward expansion was once defended.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: adherents hold the American free-market model to be the sound basis, not a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Winthrop's covenant gave a religious claim, but the mainstream view sees the US as built on ideals, not on ancestral land.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: mainstream adherents treat this as false; the sources do not discuss it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's emphasis on liberty and limited government, though religious conservatives among adherents might favour it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Reagan's farewell stresses liberty and limited government, so suppressing opposition is rejected; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: the tradition prizes religious liberty and free exercise, though Winthrop's Puritans punished dissent.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The article describes American exceptionalism as rooted in anti-colonial revolution, so ruling territories for the metropole contradicts it.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the idea is about the US and does not take up Muslim duties.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's view of lawful government and elections; the statement is not about this tradition.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on popular government, associations and local self-rule that Tocqueville praised.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from Lipset's individualism and rejection of class divisions, which cuts against structural oppression frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Adherents split along party lines; the idea does not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Adherents are split between religious conservatives and libertarian-leaning ones.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: adherents see the US as a distinct model, though some speak of bipartisan unity.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred from Lipset's individualism, work ethic and market orientation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The idea does not address Islam, and adherents are split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Winthrop grounds the community in a covenant with God while the founding tradition grounds government in consent, so adherents are split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from the stress on religious liberty and free exercise in the American tradition.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by the idea and adherents are split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Lipset's view of American anti-statism pulls against it, but the idea is not about economic design.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Reagan's farewell stresses strength and leadership abroad, so abolishing the armed forces is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Lipset's stress on competition, opportunity and individualism.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Reagan's farewell stresses strength and a leading role for the US, so staying out of blocs is contrary to the idea.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The founding rejected hereditary rule, and the American model of exceptionalism rests on a republic with elected leaders.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The strand's market-minded individualism favours private banking; the sources do not discuss mutual credit, so this is inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The mainstream patriotic version stresses national sovereignty but also free markets; the issue is not addressed, so adherents are inferred to be split.

property-franchise.rationale: American exceptionalism holds that the nation is founded on liberty and equality and popular government; the modern strand backs universal adult suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not part of the mainstream patriotic version; inferred disagreement from its individualist and religious framing.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept foreign to a strand that sees American capitalism as free and fair; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The American creed treats free speech and a free press as real rights, defended by law and not hollowed by wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The American founding celebrates government of laws, with fixed constitutional rules and independent courts, in place of arbitrary rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: Exceptionalism is built on equality and a civic, not racial, nation that welcomes immigrants; Reagan's address praises open doors.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Popular government and limited, accountable power imply openness, but the sources do not discuss open data; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious liberty is a core American ideal, so a legal limit on interfaith marriage is rejected.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Religious liberty and equality are core American ideals; shunning a minority's shops is contrary to them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Never addressed directly. Inferred from the emphasis on popular government and citizen self-rule, which makes lay deliberation congenial, though adherents differ.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Adherents are split: the idea stresses religious faith (Winthrop) but not any stance on reinterpreting doctrine; inferred, so neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Adherents split: Jeffersonian suspicion of concentrated power coexists with Reagan-style defence of wealth creation; the idea itself does not settle it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The idea is a view of the nation, not a social program; adherents on both sides of this issue claim it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The idea is bound up with religious faith and a free, religious republic, so state-promoted atheism is the opposite of it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from its patriotic respect for law, order and strength, which treats police and prisons as legitimate institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its majoritarian, individualist republic with no tradition of consociational power sharing; the idea does not address it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from Lipset-style anti-statist individualism and voluntary association, which favours private and local help over government programs.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the founding-era republican ideal of citizen legislators and popular government; adherents are not united on formal limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its attachment to the representative constitutional republic; delegable proxy voting is foreign to that tradition.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The idea does not address it; adherents split between concern for long-term survival and scepticism of global-risk framing.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split between the religious strand and mainstream denominations that ordain women.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian strand; many religious-strand adherents hold a traditional view, so this is contested.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the strand ties the vote to citizenship in a creedal republic, though adherents differ on local voting.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the strand's market-minded individualism, though it never addressed rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses property and enterprise and the US Constitution protects authors' and inventors' rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: Lipset describes an individualist, anti-statist culture that is suspicious of state-run drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: Reagan's farewell stresses strength and deterrence, so a ban on basing nuclear arms is unlikely.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses American leadership and strength abroad, which includes bases, though it holds that foreign bases in America are unthinkable.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Never addressed: the strand has no view, and adherents differ on how to treat the nation's past.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Lipset stresses opportunity and reward for effort, but the strand also defends property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the strand's individualism and gun-owning frontier tradition accept armed self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: the strand sees the US as a new covenanted nation founded on a creed, not as a people continuous from ancient origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: the patriotic strand does not hold this view, though it never addressed it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the patriotic mainstream does not use this framework, though it never addressed it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Split: the strand honours the fallen but in civic, not saintly, terms.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Winthrop's covenant sermon casts the colony as a godly mission and Reagan's era framed the Cold War as good against evil, though the strand is mostly civic.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Never addressed: the US is an immigrant nation with no diaspora doctrine.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the strand holds the nation was founded by a political covenant and constitution, with the state central from the start.

god-not-male.rationale: Split: religious adherents differ on this, and it is outside the strand's core.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the strand's religious wing holds traditional scripture, though it never addressed this.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: Lipset stresses equality of opportunity and an inclusive civic creed, which opposes ethnic economic control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the strand is built on a civic creed and a federal republic, not on one people's territory.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on liberty and civil society, which favours free association; adherents do not take this up as a distinct issue.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed; Lipset-style exceptionalism stresses the absence of a socialist class politics, but the idea itself takes no stand on this question.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents are split between local public provision and privatisation.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the American constitutional tradition of a bicameral Congress, which adherents celebrate, though the idea does not address it directly.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the individualist, property-owning ethos described by Lipset, which favours private ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold both federalist and nationalist views.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split, with traditional-family conservatives for it and others indifferent.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents are split.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents are split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between liberty-minded and security-minded views.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between liberty-minded and security-minded views.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the founding emphasis on individual rights and liberty, which treats government as existing for the person.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Winthrop's sermon and Reagan's speech frame America as a providential, religious nation, and Lipset notes its unusual religiosity.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the founding tradition of federalism with constitutionally guaranteed state powers rather than powers revocable by Congress.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents are split.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents are split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred from the civic creed of individual liberty and equality for all, which stresses shared national identity over racial group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between civic-universalist views and ancestry-based pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from Reagan's account of America as a leader that defends freedom abroad, which implies willingness to use force beyond narrow defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred: the civic version defines Americans by shared creed and open immigration, not language or ancestry, as in Reagan's beacon speech.

communal-electorates.rationale: The idea rests on one citizenship, individual liberty and rejection of Old World divisions of class and creed, so religious electorates are alien to it.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the confident, strong-nation theme in Reagan's address is at odds with fear of partition, though some patriots see foreign threats.

free-public-college.rationale: Anti-statist individualism leans against state-funded provision, though adherents across parties split on public colleges.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from anti-statist individualism and Reagan's limited government; adherents lean against new taxes, though some accept market-based measures.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Winthrop's covenant and the nation as a city upon a hill for later generations, and a stewardship tradition among patriots.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The idea of American exceptionalism does not address this and adherents are split or indifferent.

arms-reduction.rationale: Reagan's farewell stresses peace through strength, and the leadership-role strand opposes cutting arms to a minimum.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Wilsonian exceptionalists favoured open covenants while realist patriots defended secret diplomacy, so adherents split.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred: the open, free-market and global-leadership strand favours free capital flows, as Reagan's open-economy outlook shows.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the republic's ideal of a legitimate state with a monopoly of force, though the constitutional right to bear arms makes adherents wary of disarmament.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Exceptionalism stresses national strength and duty to defend the country, so a duty to refuse war runs against patriotic military service.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the anti-statist individualism the sources describe; American exceptionalists historically favour weaker unions than European models.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The idea is a view of the nation, not an economic program, and adherents split on wage supplements.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from the limited-government and anti-debt strand (Reagan-era rhetoric), though not a defining claim.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the leadership role the US claims in the existing order, which it largely built; adherents rarely favour restructuring it for developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The idea celebrates a founding constitutional order and covenant, the opposite of smashing the state; Lipset treats its liberalism as built on institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Adherents prize liberty and experiment, but the idea names no stance on a free society's economic blueprint.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from market individualism and the view that nature is used by people, though adherents do not address pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Winthrop's covenant and the civil-religion strand treat the nation as a divinely meaningful community, though adherents locate it in ideals more than blood.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from anti-statist individualism and the view that borrowers take responsibility for their choices.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The classless, unified self-image of exceptionalism rejects the internal-exploitation analysis, which is a Marxist critique.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration's creed of equal, endowed rights; adherents tend to ground rights in natural law, though bioethics is not addressed.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from market and anti-state individualism; adherents tend to favour private media over state funding.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: the Winthrop-style Christian founding vision treats the faith as true and distinctive, not as one of many equal paths.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the free-market, individualist strand of the creed, which resists guaranteed prices; farm support has had bipartisan backing, so this is contested.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the idea of the US as a leading world power that must not disarm while rivals hold weapons; Reagan-era rhetoric stressed strength.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the Lipset account of a classless, two-party-centred political culture with no tradition of a separate labor party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equality and individual rights; the idea does not address the practice directly.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on equal rights and property ownership as American founding principles.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The ideology never addressed linguistic naming; adherents have no shared view.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the individualist, property-rights and market-minded strand, which favours liability in court over agency rules; adherents are split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the republican, popular-government tradition, which has no place for hereditary or customary authority in national law.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the centrality of liberty in the creed, which adherents rank above competing goods.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Law-and-order strands favour fixed sentences, but the individualist, anti-statist strand distrusts rigid rules; adherents are split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the civic-creed view of American identity as shared language and values, with English as the common tongue.

notes: Strands differ: the interventionist leadership strand, the America First strand and the religious strand answer differently on foreign policy and social issues. Many answers are low confidence because the idea is a view of the nation rather than a full program.
